channel.title: Japan AI Monitor
channel.description: AI monitoring of Japan's political, economic and security developments

item.title: Sushi wars roll into America as Japan’s top chains face off
item.description: About 45% of Americans say they like or love sushi, according to a recent National Seafood Association report.

item.title: Takaichi launches intelligence panel, eyeing Japan’s own CIA
item.description: "Strengthening Japan's intelligence capabilities is an urgent priority," Takaichi said at the end of a closed-door meeting of the 17-member panel.

item.title: Takaichi’s reshuffle falls short of pledge on raising female representation
item.description: The prime minister pledged last year to create a "Cabinet and party leadership with as many women as in Northern European countries."

item.title: ‘Kita no Kuni kara’ screenwriter So Kuramoto dies at 91
item.description: The Tokyo native moved in 1977 to Furano, Hokkaido, where "Kita no Kuni Kara" — which depicts a family living in harmony with nature — was set.

item.title: Sony to skip CES show after Honda EV venture dropped
item.description: The company's business has shifted increasingly toward games, music and film.

item.title: Tokyo rebuts Russia’s U.N. speech accusing Japan of militarization
item.description: Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov's remarks were "factually incorrect."

item.title: Powerful U.S. missile system to be stored at Okinawa’s Kadena Air Base
item.description: The Typhon midrange weapon that has been deployed in Japan for joint military exercises will be stored at the facility indefinitely from mid-October.

item.title: Strong typhoon moves near Okinawa before possibly hitting storm-weary Kanto
item.description: The typhoon could hit areas still recovering from last week's storm, which caused extensive damage and killed at least 10 people.

item.title: Swiss franc, Japanese yen Rise as DeepSeek News Boosts Safe Havens
item.description: The Yen and Swiss Franc were stronger against the dollar as investors sought safe havens after Chinese start-up DeepSeek’s new AI model hit U.S. tech stocks.
